violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Process
violations.observation: The following raw animal foods were not properly cooked using a non-continuous cooking process: Observed a non-continuous cooking process for chicken.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods that were cooked using a non-continuous cook process shall be subject to an initial heating process that is no longer than 60 minutes in duration; immediately, after initial heating, cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified for cooked time/temperature control for safety food; after cooling, held frozenor cold; prior to sale or service, cooked using a process that heats all parts of the food to a temperature and for a time as specified under 3-401.11A-C; Cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified under 3-501.14A if not hot held, served immediately or held using time as a public health control. EHS instructed PIC to cease the non-continuous cooking process until a written procedure is submitted and approved by EHS. PIC must maintain records for each step in 6 logs for monitor the non-continuous cooking process. Alternatively, chicken must be fully cooked to 165F, then cooled to 70F within 2 hours, and further cooled to 41 within a total of 6 hours. PIC ceased the non-continuous cooking process for chicken.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: curry, duck broth, spring roll filling in WIC.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC understands all cooked/prepared foods kept for more than 24 hours must be date marked. PIC marked dates on aforementioned food items accordingly.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: observed knifes stored between 2DR prep unit and prep table at the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed, properly cleaned and stored knifes on the clean prep surface.

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Clean tableware were observed stored with the food-contact surface facing upward at the kitchen table.
violations.corrective_action: Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered/inverted. EHS discussed with management that all in-use utensil shall be stored upside down, unless they are handled with gloves. PIC stored in-use utensil upside down.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: Observed burnt out light bulbs under the hood at the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. PIC replaced burnt out light bulb during the inspection.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: observed raw chicken stored above Panang curry in WIC and raw chicken stored above chili sauce in 3 DR prep cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS discussed proper storage of raw animal food and RTE in a manner to prevent cross contamination. PIC placed raw chicken below all ready-to eat food items in both refrigeration units.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Internal condensate shelf of ice machine is not being cleaned as required.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. PIC removed ice from machine and washed, rinsed, and sanitized all internal surfaces.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: working containers of salt, sugar, pepper and etc; squeeze bottles of different types of chili sauce stored on cook line and throughout establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC labeled all working containers and squeeze bottles.

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: EHS observed manufacturer containers of white vinegar being re-used to store pre mixed Pad Thai sauce.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. EHS spoke to PIC about re-using single use manufacturer containers. PIC agreed to stop using them and switch to re-usable containers.
